local_differences: AoW owns independent JSONC configuration and file policy
AoW host modules own exclusive per-view session control, automatic restore, read-only observation and explicit takeover; ownership tokens stay outside the Rust ACP facade
Tokio and HTTP replace GPUI entities and callbacks
React components replace GPUI views
Terminal execution and terminal authentication are not advertised; legacy terminal_output metadata is supported for display-only output
History reads Zed-shaped SQLite metadata; AoW retains an independent SQLite offline transcript cache and ignores standalone JSON history

Protocol logs have service-wide count/byte limits and ended-connection eviction, thread_id/session_id/request/elicitation correlation, shared connection scope, per-thread queries across reconnections and deletion cleanup
Unknown session updates remain in snapshots and protocol logs without conversation cards
AoW Settings save events refresh the panel; configuration and execution PATH are read before connection reuse
Adapter launchers and their descendants share a dedicated process group for cleanup
AoW connection progress reports install phases, elapsed time and npm network retry codes through an additive facade query
The installed server launcher reads proxy variables from server.env at startup; Registry downloads and npm inherit them without changing macOS system plists
Settings Registry add saves JSONC and explicitly installs the adapter before new sessions are offered
The right ACP panel lists sessions; conversation content lives in central workspace tabs, with view-only close and reload restoration

Sidebar controls reuse AoW panel/list styles and conversations share its Conversation palette; persisted session links use the host tab router, with fresh-browser/mobile opening and reuse of existing floating views
React rendering ports the supported ACP branches from the pinned conversation, configuration and entry-state views; see frontend-behavior.md for function correspondence
DOM popovers, AoW Markdown and Monaco inline diffs replace native GPUI views; config search uses subsequence matching rather than upstream fuzzy ranking

Clipboard image mentions use browser editing, PNG/Base64 conversion and a bounded HTTP prompt body; file/context and attachment pickers and local prompt queueing are outside this port; authenticated live Codex and Claude prompts remain unverified
Out-of-band plan and notice snapshots preserve streamed message boundaries; notice dismissal persists across HTTP polling and reload; loading cached transcripts preserves their stored entry structure
rusqlite and a dedicated coalescing writer replace sqlez/GPUI; facade string IDs and one-workspace paths remain host adaptations, documented in persistence.md
ACP and Conversation share the host header, scrolling transcript, user/agent frames and turn navigation; an ACP-local turn adapter preserves entry rendering and its live composer

AoW API and view identity use thread_id and nullable session_id; durable preparation precedes adapter initialization, and thread metadata resolves workspace-free tab links. Snapshots use the current identity fields without aliases; saved tab descriptors require thread_id

AoW packages, module paths, CSS and DOM events use ACP names. Configuration and runtime storage are read only from the active ACP paths; former directories are not migrated. The facade, SQLite schema and thread identity are unchanged; upstream provenance is retained in this manifest.

Plan and request cards follow the pinned Zed structure with AoW Conversation colors, typography and a shared 900px content column; owner-controlled plan clearing persists through snapshot polling and reload without canceling execution

Successful live ACP prompts invoke the optional host turn-completed callback once; AoW shares its Terminal notification dispatcher, page/IM settings and unread queue, with ACP thread destinations and conservative response-usage deltas

Streaming persistence queues shared session references and captures bodies after a one-second coalescing window; generation/revision HTTP deltas carry entry replacements and text/terminal appends, while old terminal-output metadata is normalized on load. Zed uses GPUI events and virtual lists; AoW retains its offline body cache and React layout.

Browser history defaults to turn overviews; process bodies use scoped lazy reads and deltas only while expanded. Collapse unmounts details and releases their data and requests. Virtual lists and database repartitioning remain deferred.

Sidebar recency carries the existing interacted_at column through snapshots and desktop/mobile lists. Only accepted user submissions advance it; imports and legacy hydration freeze historical update time as their baseline. Snapshot updated_at and revision still track all state changes.

SDK 3.4.0/schema 1.12.0 is newer than the recorded Zed source baseline. Compaction chunks follow the new receive-order contract, and initialization rejects protocol versions other than v1. Subagent and system-prompt behavior remain outside this upgrade.
